title: Goll voish boayl gys boayl
description: Ten short stories about getting around: a train ride to a wedding in Ramsey, the ferry to Liverpool, a stolen boat found by a detective, Swiss trains, a school trip on the steam train, a flight to China, a students' electric vehicle, the electric railway to Laxey, a walk to a reservoir in the hills and a flight to Dublin.

lessons.title: Y cuirrey
lessons.summary: In spring Gwyneth, who lives in Peel, gets an invitation to her friend Tara's wedding in Ramsey on a Friday; on Thursday she buys a gift, on the day her father phones to ask if she is ready, she waits on the wrong side of the line for the electric train and still reaches the church in time.
lessons.text:
Ayns yn arragh, hooar Gwyneth Lloyd cuirrey 'sy phost. Va'n cuirrey veih e carrey Tara. Va Tara goll dy phoosey Jeheiney, ayns y cheeill veg ayns Rhumsaa. Ta Gwyneth cummal ayns Pheeil, as cha nel carr eck. “Hem dys Doolish er y bus, as eisht hem dys Rhumsaa er y traen lectragh,” dooyrt ee rish e ayr.

Jerdein, hie Gwyneth dys ny shappyn ayns Pheeil dy chionnaghey gioot. Ren ee shirrey son traa liauyr. Ec y jerrey, ghow ee cappan mooar gorrym as blaaghyn buigh er. “She gioot mie eh shoh,” dooyrt fer y shapp. “Ta sleih kinjagh laccal cappanyn noa.” Hug Gwyneth y gioot ayns pabyr jiarg.

Jeheiney, ec shiaght er y chlag, hug e ayr eam er Gwyneth er y çhellvane. “Vel oo ullee?” dooyrt eh.

“Ta mee bunnys ullee,” dooyrt ee. “Ta mee cur my chooat orrym.”

“Vel dty ghioot ayd, as dty chuirrey?” dooyrt eh.

“Ta,” dooyrt ee.

“Immee nish, my ta,” dooyrt e ayr. “Ta'n bus goll ec lieh oor lurg shiaght.”

Hie Gwyneth dys Doolish er y bus, as eisht dys stashoon y traen lectragh. Hass ee ec y raad yiarn. Haink traen er y lhiattee elley. Row Gwyneth er y lhiattee cooie? Cha row. Dooyrt ben veg dy row traenyn Rhumsaa goll veih'n lhiattee elley.

Roie Gwyneth dys y lhiattee elley lesh y gioot, as hie ee stiagh 'sy traen. Hug ee eam er Tara: “Ta mee er y traen nish. Ta mee anmagh, agh hig mee!”

Hie y traen dy moal raad y slyst, as va'n arragh aalin er dagh lhiattee: blaaghyn buigh 'sy thalloo, as eayin aegey 'sy vagher. Haink Gwyneth dys y cheeill ayns Rhumsaa ec y traa cheddin as Tara hene.

Lurg y phoosey, ghow Tara yn gioot. “Gura mie ayd son dty ghioot,” dooyrt ee, “as son çheet foddey.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre hooar Gwyneth 'sy phost?
Hooar ee cuirrey veih Tara.
Cre'n laa va Tara poosey?
Va Tara poosey Jeheiney.
Cre ren Gwyneth Jerdein?
Ren ee gioot y chionnaghey ayns Pheeil.
Cre dooyrt e ayr er y çhellvane?
Dooyrt eh, “Vel oo ullee?”
Row Gwyneth er y lhiattee cooie?
Cha row. Va traenyn Rhumsaa goll veih'n lhiattee elley.

lessons.title: Er y lhong dys Lerphoyll
lessons.summary: Barry takes his grandson Jasper on the ferry to Liverpool: the weather is foggy, the boat is full of visitors, Jasper's stomach is sick until they eat potatoes, the wind throws his hat into the sea, and Barry tells him how a sailor once saved a man from drowning.
lessons.text:
Ta Barry Scarffe goll dys Lerphoyll er y lhong marish mac e vac, Jasper. Ta Jasper queig bleeaney jeig d'eash, as she yn chied turrys echey er lhong. Ta ram keayrtee er y lhong. Haink ny keayrtee shoh dys Ellan Vannin son ny ratçhalyn, as nish t'ad goll thie. Ta keayrtagh mooar veih Nalbin ny hassoo rish Jasper, as ta edd gorrym er.

Va'n emshir çhiu ec y toshiaght. Cha row Jasper abyl Doolish y akin. “Cre'n fa nagh vel mee fakin yn ellan?” dooyrt eh. “Er y fa dy vel yn emshir çhiu,” dooyrt e shennayr. “Ta'n kay ro çhiu dy akin red erbee.”

Lurg oor, va geay lajer ayn, as va'n lhong goll seose as sheese er ny tonnyn. Va pian ayns gailley Jasper. “Ta my ghailley ching,” dooyrt eh. Hie eh magh dy ghoaill aer.

Va'n geay feayr er cleayshyn Jasper. “Cur dty edd ort,” dooyrt Barry. “Bee dty chleayshyn feer feayr 'sy gheay shoh.” Hug Jasper yn edd echey er e chione, agh ghow y geay eh. Ren y geay yn edd y hilgey ayns y cheayn.

“Cha nel shin abyl dty edd y haue nish,” dooyrt Barry. “Ta'n keayn ro vooar.”

Va Jasper tilgey arran da ny ushagyn mooiragh. “Ta ushagyn mooiragh cummal er y cheayn son y chooid smoo jeh'n vlein,” dooyrt Barry. “T'ad çheet gys y thalloo ynrican son nyn oohyn.”

Eisht, ghow ad bee 'sy shamyr vee: eeast as praaseyn. Lurg ny praaseyn, va gailley Jasper ny share.

Dooyrt Barry: “Tra va mee aeg, va mee gobbraghey er lhong myr shoh. Oie dy row, huitt dooinney ayns y cheayn. Va'n ushtey feer feayr, as v'eh bunnys baiht. Hug shiaulteyr aeg y laue echey stiagh 'syn ushtey, as ren eh y dooinney y haue. Cha row'n dooinney baiht. Lurg shen, hug y dooinney gioot da'n shiaulteyr dagh Nollick.”

Ec y jerrey, va'n emshir glen, as honnick Jasper Lerphoyll.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta er y lhong?
Ta ram keayrtee er y lhong.
Cre'n fa nagh row Jasper fakin Doolish?
Er y fa dy row yn emshir çhiu.
Cre hie ayns y cheayn?
Hie edd Jasper ayns y cheayn.
Cre ghow ad 'sy shamyr vee?
Ghow ad eeast as praaseyn.
Row'n dooinney baiht?
Cha row. Ren shiaulteyr aeg eh y haue.

lessons.title: Yn baatey caillt
lessons.summary: Someone takes Shona's small boat from the harbour at Port St Mary; a detective searches the harbours along the coast and finds it in Peel with a long scratch and damage to the side, the young thief is punished in court, and Shona's lawyer gets her the money for the repairs.
lessons.text:
Ta baatey beg ec Shona Gorry. T'eh ayns y phurt ayns Purt Çhiarn. Dagh Jesarn, ta Shona goll magh er y cheayn 'sy vaatey eck.

Laa dy row, hie Shona sheese dys y phurt, as cha row'n baatey ayn. Hug ee eam er y pholasee. Haink cronneyder, Glyn Hale, dys y phurt. “Vel docamadyn ayd son y baatey?” dooyrt eh. Hug Shona ny docamadyn da. V'ad screeuit ayns ennym Shona, as va ennym y vaatey orroo.

Ren y cronneyder ronsee er y phurt. Eisht, ren eh ronsee er ny puirt elley raad y slyst. Va fys echey dy row ram baatyn caillt 'sy vlein shoh. “Nee'm y cooish shoh y feayshil,” dooyrt eh.

Lurg daa laa, hooar y cronneyder y baatey ayns Pheeil. Va jeeyl er y vaatey. Va screeb liauyr er y lhiattee echey. Honnick Shona yn jeeyl as y screeb. “Quoi ren shen?” dooyrt ee.

Va feanish ayn: shenn eeasteyr veih Pheeil. Va'n shenn dooinney barrantagh. Honnick eh guilley aeg çheet stiagh 'sy phurt lesh y baatey. Ren y guilley y baatey y screeb er ny claghyn. Va'n cronneyder er feayshil y chooish.

Va'n guilley er ny chur roish y briw ayns Doolish. Va leighder ec Shona. Dooyrt y leighder dy row'n feanish barrantagh, as dy row'n jeeyl er y vaatey mooar. Hug y leighder docamad da'n briw: towse jeh'n argid son y baatey y chur kiart reesht.

Ren y briw y guilley y cherree. Hug ee sare da: dy obbraghey 'sy phurt son three meeghyn, as argid y chur da Shona son y jeeyl. “Ta mee kerree oo,” dooyrt y briw, “son dy ghow oo baatey nagh row lhiat.”

Lurg y sare, ren leighder Shona yn argid y gheddyn. Ta'n baatey glen reesht, gyn screeb erbee.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ren y cronneyder 'sy toshiaght?
Ren eh ronsee er y phurt.
Cre'n boayl hooar eh y baatey?
Hooar eh y baatey ayns Pheeil.
Cre va er lhiattee y vaatey?
Va screeb liauyr er y lhiattee.
Cre hug y leighder da'n briw?
Hug eh docamad da'n briw.
Cre'n sare hug y briw da'n guilley?
Hug ee sare da dy obbraghey 'sy phurt son three meeghyn.

lessons.title: Traenyn ny h-Elveeish
lessons.summary: Marion travels by train through Switzerland to find the village of an ancestor: she buys a single ticket, learns that the country is a federation of twenty-six cantons, admires the size of the mountains and the trains' fame for running on time, and shows a printed copy of an old document in the village.
lessons.text:
Ta Marion Hughes goll dys yn Elveeish er y traen. Va sheanseyr eck ruggit ayns balley beg ayns shen, as t'ee laccal y balley y akin. T'ee feer jeean. Ta coip eck jeh docamad shenn: lettyr veih'n sheanseyr eck, screeuit ayns 1850. Ta'n choip phrentit er pabyr bane.

Ayns stashoon Zürich, ren Marion tiggad y chionnaghey. “Tiggad singyl dys Bern,” dooyrt ee. “Singyl? Nagh vel oo çheet thie reesht?” dooyrt y ven. “Cha nel fys aym foast,” dooyrt Marion. Hug y ven tiggad singyl phrentit da Marion.

Er y traen, va dooinney shenn ny hoie rish Marion. “She conast yn Elveeish,” dooyrt eh. “Ta shey cantoonyn as feed 'sy conast. Ta reiltys hene ec dagh cantoon, as ta'n conast reill y çheer ooilley.” Ta'n balley ayns cantoon Bern.

Va'n traen goll trooid ny sleityn. Va Marion fakin mooad ny sleityn. “Cha nel sleityn jeh'n mooad shoh ayns Ellan Vannin,” dooyrt ee. Va'n traen çheet ec y traa kiart dys dagh stashoon. “Ta foaynoo mooar ec ny traenyn shoh,” dooyrt y dooinney. “Ta foaynoo oc son shen: t'ad kinjagh çheet ec y traa.”

'Sy valley, hie Marion dys oik y valley. Hug ee y choip da'n ven 'syn oik, Ursula Kunz. Va Ursula Kunz jeean dy yannoo shen. Ren ee jeeaghyn ayns lioaryn shenn, as hooar ee ennym sheanseyr Marion ayns lioar. “Shoh yn ennym echey,” dooyrt ee. “Va'n thie echey faggys da'n cheeill.” Hug ee coip phrentit jeh'n duillag da Marion.

Va'n thie foast ayn, beg as bane. “Ta'n thie shoh jeh'n mooad cheddin as y thie aym hene,” dooyrt Marion rish hene.

Lurg shen, hie Marion dys y stashoon reesht. Ren ee tiggad singyl elley y chionnaghey: v'ee goll dys cantoon elley.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta Marion goll dys yn Elveeish?
Va sheanseyr eck ruggit ayns balley beg ayns shen.
Cre'n tiggad ren ee kionnaghey?
Ren ee tiggad singyl y chionnaghey.
Vel ram cantoonyn 'sy conast?
Ta. Ta shey cantoonyn as feed 'sy conast.
Cre'n foaynoo ta ec ny traenyn?
T'ad kinjagh çheet ec y traa.
Cre hug Ursula Kunz da Marion?
Hug ee coip phrentit jeh'n duillag da Marion.

lessons.title: Y turrys scoill
lessons.summary: Nigel takes his class on the steam train to a big garden in the south: he shows how water climbs through the xylem, how bees pollinate the tiny florets, a dock leaf soothes a girl's nettle sting, they see algae on the pond and acanthus leaves like the decorative ones on Greek temples, plant seeds in clay pots and pick apples.
lessons.text:
Ta Nigel Baxter ny ynseyder ayns bunscoill ayns Doolish. Jerdein, ghow eh y rang echey er turrys scoill. Hie ad er y traen gaal veih Doolish dys garey mooar 'sy jiass. Ta'n traen gaal shenn as moal, agh s'mie lesh ny paitçhyn eh.

'Sy garey, ghow Nigel blaa bane, as hug eh eh ayns ushtey gorrym. “Jeeagh er y blaa shoh ec y jerrey jeh'n laa,” dooyrt eh.

Eisht, hie ad dys ny blaaghyn. Va shellanyn goll veih blaa dys blaa. “Ta ny shellanyn jannoo pollnaghey,” dooyrt Nigel. “T'ad cur stoo veih un vlaa dys blaa elley. Gyn pollnaghey, cha bee mess ayn.” Ghow eh blaa buigh 'sy laue echey. “Jeeagh: cha nel shoh un vlaa. Ta ram blaagyn beggey ayn. Ta dagh blaag ny vlaa beg ayns hene.”

Va caillin 'sy rang enmyssit Fern. Hug Fern e laue er lus undaagagh, as va pian eck. Ghow Nigel duillag vooar ghlass. “Shoh duillag cabbag,” dooyrt eh. “Ta cabbag kinjagh gaase faggys da'n undaagagh.” Hug eh y duillag cabbag er laue y chaillin, as va'n pian ny sloo.

Ayns y logh, va algey glass er yn ushtey. “Ta algey ny lus feer veg,” dooyrt Nigel. “Ta ny eeast beaghey er algey.”

Ec dorrys y thie glass, va lus mooar lesh duillagyn liauyrey. “Shoh jialg,” dooyrt Nigel. “Ayns y Ghreag, keayrt dy row, va sleih jannoo duillagyn jialg jeh clagh er y çhiamble. V'ad jesheenagh: cha row ad ayn agh son dy ve aalin.” Honnick ny paitçhyn jalloo jeh çhiamble shenn as duillagyn jialg jesheenagh er.

Lurg shen, ren dagh paitçhey rass y chur ayns saagh cray. “Ta cray mie son lossreeyn,” dooyrt Nigel. “Ta'n cray freayll yn ushtey.” Ghow Fern e saagh cray thie lesh.

Ec y jerrey, ghow ny paitçhyn ooyllyn veih ny billaghyn ooyl. Eisht, honnick ad y blaa bane. Va'n blaa gorrym nish! “Hie'n ushtey gorrym seose trooid y sylem,” dooyrt Nigel. “Ta'n sylem myr feddanyn beggey. T'eh gymmyrkey ushtey veih ny fraueyn dys ny duillagyn as ny blaaghyn.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n aght hie yn rang dys y garey?
Hie ad er y traen gaal.
Cre ta ny shellanyn jannoo?
T'ad jannoo pollnaghey.
Cre hug Nigel er laue Fern?
Hug eh duillag cabbag er laue Fern.
Cre va er yn ushtey 'sy logh?
Va algey glass er yn ushtey.
Cre'n fa va'n blaa bane gorrym ec y jerrey?
Hie'n ushtey gorrym seose trooid y sylem.

lessons.title: Turrys dys ny Sheen
lessons.summary: Bryony flies from London to Beijing to study at a college for a year: she sleeps on the long flight, a man from Hong Kong tells her about colonial rule there and the language most people speak, and in Beijing she finds that Chinese adjectives never change but the tones are a real difficulty.
lessons.text:
Ta Bryony Turner veih Doolish goll dys ny Sheen. Bee ee ynsaghey Sheenish son blein ayns colaashtey ayns Beijing. Va yeearree eck rieau dy ynsaghey Sheenish. Tra v'ee aeg, honnick ee scannane mychione ny Sheen, as dooyrt ee rish e moir: “Ta mee laccal Sheenish y loayrt!” Nish ta'n yeearree shen çheet dy ve firrinagh.

Hie Bryony er etlan veih Lunnin. Va'n turrys feer liauyr: un oor jeig. Ren ee cadley son shey ooryn. Lurg y cadley, va dooinney ny hoie rish. Va'n dooinney, Wei Chen, veih Hong Kong.

“Vel Hong Kong ayns Deynphobblaght ny Sheen?” dooyrt Bryony.

“Ta, nish,” dooyrt Wei. “Agh roish 1997, va Hong Kong fo reill y Reeriaght Unnaneysit. Va shen coloinaghys. Ta skeeal coloinaghys liauyr ayns yn ayrn shoh jeh'n theihll. Nish, ta Hong Kong ayns y deynphobblaght, agh ta reill hene echey foast.”

“Vel sleih Hong Kong loayrt Sheenish?” dooyrt Bryony.

“Ta formley y phobble loayrt Yue, Sheenish Hong Kong,” dooyrt Wei. “Ta formley y phobble ayns y deynphobblaght loayrt Mandarinish, yn Sheenish t'ou ynsaghey.”

Ayns Beijing, hie Bryony dys y colaashtey er y traen fo-halloo. Va ny cowraghyn ooilley ayns Sheenish. Va doilleeid eck lhaih ny cowraghyn.

Er y chied laa 'sy cholaashtey, dooyrt yn ynseyder, Ven Lin: “Cha nel marennym 'sy Sheenish caghlaa myr marennym 'sy Ghaelg. Ta'n marennym kinjagh yn red cheddin.” “Ayns Gaelg, ta'n marennym caghlaa ny keayrtyn: ben vie, dooinney mie,” dooyrt Bryony.

Agh va doilleeid elley ayn. 'Sy Sheenish, ta'n coraa goll seose as sheese tra t'ou loayrt fockle, as ta'n fockle caghlaa lesh. “She shoh yn doilleeid smoo da formley ny studeyryn,” dooyrt Ven Lin.

'Syn oie, roish y cadley, screeu ee e chied fockle Sheenish 'sy lioar eck.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta Bryony goll dys ny Sheen?
T'ee goll dy ynsaghey Sheenish ayns colaashtey.
Cre ren ee er yn etlan?
Ren ee cadley son shey ooryn.
Row Hong Kong ayns y deynphobblaght roish 1997?
Cha row. V'eh fo reill y Reeriaght Unnaneysit.
Cre ta formley pobble Hong Kong loayrt?
T'ad loayrt Yue.
Vel y marennym caghlaa 'sy Sheenish?
Cha nel. Ta'n marennym kinjagh yn red cheddin.

lessons.title: Y carbyd lectragh
lessons.summary: Aled and Cora, two college students, build a small electric vehicle for a race on the promenade: Cora does the mathematics on calculators, the first vehicle is too heavy, the college gives a positive answer when they ask for money, Aled reads about the inventor of an early electric carriage and dreams of planetary rovers, and their attractive vehicle wins a sum of money under the sodium lamps.
lessons.text:
Ta Aled Palmer as Cora Grant nyn studeyryn ayns Doolish. T'ad troggal carbyd lectragh beg son ratçhal. Bee'n ratçhal ayns Doolish ec jerrey y vlein, 'syn oie, raad y traie.

Ta Cora mie er maddaght. Ren ee yn vaddaght son y carbyd: cre cha trome as veagh eh, as cre cha tappee as oddagh eh goll. Ren ee ymmyd jeh daa earrooder, agh va feme eck er earrooderyn ny share. “Ta'n vaddaght shoh doillee,” dooyrt ee. “Ta ny earrooderyn ain ro shenn.”

Hie ad dys stiureyder y cholaashtey. “Vel shiu abyl argid y chur dooin son earrooderyn noa?” dooyrt Aled. Hooar ad freggyrt jarrooagh. “She freggyrt jarrooagh t'ayn!” dooyrt Cora. Ghow ad earrooderyn noa.

Va'n chied carbyd jeant jeh yiarn, as v'eh ro ghloutagh. Va'n carbyd gloutagh feer voal. “Cre'n fa t'eh cha gloutagh?” dooyrt Aled. “Er y fa dy vel y yiarn ro hrome,” dooyrt Cora. Ren ad carbyd noa jeh fuygh as stoo ny sloo trome.

Ayns lioar ayns y lioarlann, lhaih Aled mychione ynlaghteyr veih Nalbin, Robert Anderson. She eshyn crootagh jeh carbyd lectragh ayns ny 1830yn. “V'eh ny ynlaghteyr mie,” dooyrt Aled, “agh va'n carbyd echey feer ghloutagh.” Ta Aled laccal ve ny ynlaghteyr hene. Laa ennagh, t'eh laccal gobbraghey er carbyd planaidagh: carbyd ta goll er planaid elley. “Veagh y carbyd shoh ro ghloutagh son carbyd planaidagh,” dooyrt eh.

Ren Cora jalloo jeh'n carbyd noa. She ish crootagh yn jalloo. Va'n carbyd beg as tayrnagh, lesh daah gorrym as bane. “T'eh tayrnagh!” dooyrt Aled.

Oie y ratçhal, va soilsheyderyn sodjum er y raad. Ta soilshey buigh ec sodjum. Fo ny soilsheyderyn sodjum, va'n carbyd oc ny smoo tappee na dagh carbyd elley. Hooar ad yn aundyr: sym mooar argid. Hug ad lieh jeh'n sym da'n cholaashtey, son carbyd y vlein noa.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Cora mie er?
T'ee mie er maddaght.
Cre'n freggyrt hooar ad veih'n stiureyder?
Hooar ad freggyrt jarrooagh.
Cre'n fa va'n chied carbyd moal?
V'eh ro ghloutagh.
Quoi va Robert Anderson?
V'eh ny ynlaghteyr veih Nalbin.
Cre hooar ad ec y ratçhal?
Hooar ad sym mooar argid.

lessons.title: Er y traen dys Laksaa
lessons.summary: Elliot takes his grandmother Edna north on the electric railway to Laxey: they climb the spiral stairs of the great wheel, read the names engraved on a stone, see the record of the miners kept in the museum and the metal-bearing rocks, and Edna tells him an old giant tale from Manx mythology.
lessons.text:
Ta Elliot Shaw goll lesh e shenn-voir, Edna, dys Laksaa. T'ad goll er y traen lectragh veih Doolish. Ta Laksaa ayns yn ayrn twoaieagh jeh'n ellan, as ta'n raad yiarn goll raad y slyst twoaieagh. Va mian er Edna rieau dy akin y Queeyl Vooar reesht. Hie ee dys Laksaa keayrt tra v'ee aeg.

Ta'n Queeyl Vooar freaylt ec Ellan Vannin. Ta sleih freaylt y queeyl son dy vel ee scanshoil 'sy shennaghys. Ta raad caslagh goll mygeayrt as seose gys y mullagh. Hie Elliot as Edna seose y raad caslagh dy moal. Veih'n mullagh, honnick ad y glion ooilley.

Faggys da'n queeyl, va clagh vooar. Va enmyn grainnit er y chlagh: enmyn ny h-obbreeyn hooar baase ayns ny meainyn. “Ta'n ennym ain grainnit ayns shen,” dooyrt Edna. “Va sheanseyr ain gobbraghey 'sy veain.” Honnick Elliot yn ennym grainnit: Alfred Shaw, 1897.

Ayns y thie-tashtee, va rheam lheead dy reddyn: greieyn, eaddagh as jallooyn. Va lioar vooar ayn, as va ennym dagh obbree er ny recortyssey ayn. “Ta'n lioar shoh recortyssey ennym as eash dagh dooinney,” dooyrt yn ven 'sy thie-tashtee. Va rheam mooar dy chreggyn ayn neesht. “Ta ny creggyn shoh meainagh,” dooyrt ee. “Ta leoie as argid 'sy chreg veainagh shoh.”

Er y traen thie, ren Edna skeeal y insh veih feayn-skeealleydaght Vannin. “Ayns y skeealleydaght shenn, va foawr mooar cummal 'sy twoaie,” dooyrt ee. “Va mian er y foawr dy ghoaill yn ellan ooilley. Ren y foawr clagh vooar y hilgey 'sy cheayn. Ta'n clagh foast ayn.”

“Vel skeealleydaght Vannin firrinagh?” dooyrt Elliot.

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Edna, “agh ta'n skeeal shen freaylt foast, as she shen ny smoo scanshoil.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n boayl ta Laksaa?
Ta Laksaa ayns yn ayrn twoaieagh jeh'n ellan.
Cre'n aght hie ad gys mullagh y queeyl?
Hie ad seose y raad caslagh.
Cre va grainnit er y chlagh?
Va enmyn ny h-obbreeyn grainnit er y chlagh.
Cre ta'n lioar vooar recortyssey?
T'ee recortyssey ennym as eash dagh dooinney.
Cre va mian er y foawr?
Va mian er dy ghoaill yn ellan ooilley.

lessons.title: Er cass dys y doour
lessons.summary: Kenneth walks up the glen to the reservoir in the hills with his daughter's dog: his leg starts to hurt, he drinks from a spring and an old well when his throat is dry, almost changes his mind and turns back, sees his own shadow on the mist, a rare phenomenon, and carries the tired dog down.
lessons.text:
Ta Kenneth Rowe cummal ayns Sulby. Jesarn, hie eh er cass seose y glion dys y doour 'sy slieau. Ghow eh moddey e inneen marish, moddey beg enmyssit Bran. Ta'n doour mooar as dowin. T'eh freayll ushtey son ny baljyn.

Va'n raad liauyr, as va'n çhiassid mooar. Lurg oor, va pian ayns lurgey Kenneth. “Ta my lurgey ching,” dooyrt eh rish Bran. Cha row bree ec y moddey boght neesht. Va scoarnagh Kenneth çhirrym, as cha row ushtey echey.

Haink ad gys farrane beg ec oirr y raad. Va'n ushtey glen as feayr. Ren Kenneth as Bran giu veih'n farrane. Va scoarnagh Kenneth ny share.

Ny sodjey seose, va tobbyr shenn. Va sleih goll dys y tobbyr shoh rish ymmodee keeadyn blein. Va'n tobbyr shoh enmyssit er noo. Ghow Kenneth ushtey ass y tobbyr ayns e laueyn.

Agh va lurgey Kenneth foast ching. Ren eh caghlaa e aigney. “Hem thie,” dooyrt eh. Eisht, ren eh caghlaa e aigney reesht: “Cha nel. Ta'n doour faggys nish.”

Ec y doour, va kay ayn. Va'n ghrian cooyl Kenneth, as honnick eh scaa mooar er y kay, as kiarkyl dy hollys mygeayrt y scaa. “She phenomenon t'ayn,” dooyrt eh rish hene. Lhaih eh mychione y phenomenon shoh ayns lioar keayrt. Ta'n phenomenon shoh feer neuchadjin. Cha nel eh ry-akin agh tra ta'n ghrian cooyl dooinney as kay roish.

Er y raad sheese, cha row bree ec Bran dy hooyl. Va'n moddey boght ny lhie er y thalloo. “Ymmyrk mee!” va'n moddey jeeaghyn dy ghra. Ghow Kenneth y moddey seose. V'eh ymmyrkit sheese y glion ayns laueyn Kenneth. “Ymmyrkee mee oo thie,” dooyrt Kenneth rish y moddey.

'Syn oie, dooyrt inneen Kenneth: “Cre'n fa nagh vel bree ec Bran?” “Ren eh shooyl dys y doour,” dooyrt Kenneth, “as v'eh ymmyrkit thie ayns my laueyn.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n boayl hie Kenneth er cass?
Hie eh dys y doour 'sy slieau.
Cre va ching?
Va lurgey Kenneth ching.
Cre ren eh tra va'n scoarnagh echey çhirrym?
Ren eh giu veih'n farrane.
Cre honnick eh er y kay?
Honnick eh scaa mooar as kiarkyl dy hollys: phenomenon.
Cre'n aght haink Bran thie?
V'eh ymmyrkit thie ayns laueyn Kenneth.

lessons.title: Yn etlan dys Divlyn
lessons.summary: Siobhan flies from the island to Dublin for a meeting of language organisations: she loses and finds her key, reads a reader's letter in the newspaper on the plane, prepares a game about masculine and feminine words for children, and at the meeting the campaign that advises parents to speak the language at home is approved with raised hands.
lessons.text:
Ta Siobhan Kearney gobbraghey son reagheydys ayns Ellan Vannin. Ta'n reagheydys gobbraghey son y Ghaelg. Jeheiney, t'ee goll dys Divlyn er yn etlan. Bee çhaglym ayn ayns Divlyn: reagheydyssyn veih Nerin, Nalbin as Ellan Vannin. Ta ny reagheydyssyn shoh gobbraghey son Gaelg, Yernish as Gaelg Nalbin.

'Sy thie, cha row Siobhan abyl yn ogher eck y gheddyn. “Cre'n boayl ta my ogher?” dooyrt ee. Ren ee shirrey son yn ogher son tammylt. Ec y jerrey, hooar ee yn ogher ayns e cooat.

Er yn etlan, va pabyr naight ec Siobhan. Lhaih ee lettyr veih lhaihder. Va'n lhaihder gra: “Cha nel Baarle ny noid da'n Ghaelg. Ta noid smoo y Ghaelg ayns y thie: sleih nagh vel loayrt ee rish nyn baitçhyn.” “Ta'n lhaihder shoh kiart,” dooyrt Siobhan rish hene.

Eisht, ren Siobhan cloie son paitçhyn y aarlaghey. 'Sy chloie, ta'n paitçhey gra my ta fockle firrynagh ny bwoirrinagh. “Ta ‘dooinney’ firrynagh, as ta ‘ben’ bwoirrinagh,” screeu ee. “Ta ‘lhaihder’ firrynagh. Ta ‘ogher’ bwoirrinagh.” Ta'n chloie shoh son y faghtys noa.

Ec y çhaglym, loayr Siobhan mychione y faghtys. Ta'n faghtys coyrlaghey paarantyn dy loayrt Gaelg rish ny paitçhyn oc ec y thie. “Ta'n faghtys coyrlaghey dy loayrt Gaelg dagh laa, ga dy vel oo loayrt agh beggan,” dooyrt ee. Lhaih ee lettyr y lhaihder da ny reagheydyssyn.

“Quoi ta son y faghtys?” dooyrt dooinney ec y çhaglym. “Yrjee nyn laueyn.” Ren dagh persoon e laue y yrjee. Ren ny reagheydyssyn veih Nerin as Nalbin coardail dy yannoo faghtys cosoylagh ayns nyn çheeraghyn hene.

Er yn etlan thie, va Siobhan smooinaghtyn er y lhaihder as y lettyr echey. Ren ee screeu lettyr da'n phabyr hene: “Ta'n noid ain ayns y thie, agh ta'n cooney ayns y thie neesht.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta Siobhan goll dys Divlyn?
T'ee goll dys çhaglym reagheydyssyn.
Cre'n boayl hooar ee yn ogher eck?
Hooar ee yn ogher ayns e cooat.
Cre dooyrt y lhaihder 'sy lettyr?
Dooyrt eh nagh vel Baarle ny noid da'n Ghaelg.
Vel ‘lhaihder’ firrynagh ny bwoirrinagh?
Ta ‘lhaihder’ firrynagh.
Cre ta'n faghtys coyrlaghey?
T'eh coyrlaghey paarantyn dy loayrt Gaelg rish ny paitçhyn ec y thie.
